The '''2024–25 La Liga''', also known as '''La Liga EA Sports'''<ref>{{cite news |title=EA Sports & LaLiga Announce Expansive New Partnership With EA SPORTS FC as Title Sponsor of All LaLiga Competitions |url=https://news.ea.com/press-releases/press-releases-details/2022/EA-SPORTS--LaLiga-Announce-Expansive-New-Partnership-With-EA-SPORTS-FC-as-Title-Sponsor-of-All-LaLiga-Competitions/default.aspx |publisher=Electronic Arts |date=2 August 2022 |access-date=27 April 2023 |archive-date=23 June 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260623155025/https://news.ea.com/press-releases/press-releases-details/2022/EA-SPORTS--LaLiga-Announce-Expansive-New-Partnership-With-EA-SPORTS-FC-as-Title-Sponsor-of-All-LaLiga-Competitions/default.aspx |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=EA Sports FC will be the title sponsor of all LaLiga competitions |url=https://www.laliga.com/en-GB/news/ea-sports-fc-will-be-the-title-sponsor-of-all-laliga-competitions |publisher=La Liga |date=2 August 2022 |access-date=14 May 2023 |archive-date=23 June 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260623155742/https://www.laliga.com/en-GB/news/ea-sports-fc-will-be-the-title-sponsor-of-all-laliga-competitions |url-status=live }}</ref> due to sponsorship reasons, was the 94th season of [[La Liga]], Spain's premier football competition. It commenced on 15 August 2024 and concluded on 25 May 2025. [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] were the defending champions, having won their 36th title the previous season. The fixture schedule was announced on 18 June 2024.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.relevo.com/futbol/calendario-laliga-2425-sorteara-proximo-20240614122820-nt.html|title=El calendario de LaLiga 24/25 se sorteará el próximo martes|website=Relevo|date=14 June 2024|access-date=31 March 2025|language=es|archive-date=14 June 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240614111143/https://www.relevo.com/futbol/calendario-laliga-2425-sorteara-proximo-20240614122820-nt.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 15 May 2025, [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] officially secured their 28th title with two matches to spare following a 2–0 win against [[Derbi Barceloní|city rivals]] [[RCD Espanyol|Espanyol]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.laliga.com/en-GB/news/fc-barcelona-crowned-champions-of-laliga-ea-sports-2024-25|title=FC Barcelona crowned champions of LALIGA EA SPORTS 2024/25|publisher=La Liga|date=15 May 2025|access-date=15 May 2025|archive-date=20 May 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250520183817/https://www.laliga.com/en-GB/news/fc-barcelona-crowned-champions-of-laliga-ea-sports-2024-25|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Promotion and relegation (pre-season)===
A total of twenty teams contest the league, including seventeen sides from the [[2023–24 La Liga|2023–24 season]] and three promoted from the [[2023–24 Segunda División]]. This includes the two top teams from the Segunda División, and the winners of the [[2024 Segunda División play-offs|promotion play-offs]].

;Teams relegated to Segunda División
The first team to be relegated from La Liga were [[UD Almería|Almería]], after a 1–3 loss to [[Getafe CF|Getafe]] on 27 April 2024, ending their two-year stay in top tier. The second team to be relegated was [[Granada CF|Granada]], following [[RCD Mallorca|Mallorca]]’s 1–0 win against [[UD Las Palmas|Las Palmas]], suffering immediate relegation. The third and final team relegated to Segunda was [[Cádiz CF|Cádiz]], after a 0–0 draw against Las Palmas on 19 May 2024, ending their four-year stay in the top tier.
;Teams promoted from Segunda División
On 26 May 2024, [[Real Valladolid|Valladolid]] became the first side to mathematically be automatically promoted, assured of a return to the top flight following a 3–2 win against [[Villarreal CF B|Villarreal B]], thus returning after a single season absence.<ref>{{cite news |date=26 May 2024 |title=Ronaldo's Valladolid promoted back to La Liga |url=https://www.thescore.com/topsn/news/2918510 |access-date=25 June 2024 |website=theScore}}</ref> The second and final team to earn automatic promotion was [[CD Leganés|Leganés]], following a 2–0 win against [[Elche CF|Elche]] on 2 June 2024, thus returning after a four-season absence and also being promoted to the top flight for the second time in their history.<ref>{{cite news |date=2 June 2024 |title=Leganes win Spanish second division to reach La Liga |url=https://www.thescore.com/espcr/news/2921658 |access-date=25 June 2024 |website=theScore}}</ref> The third and final team to be promoted was [[RCD Espanyol|Espanyol]], following their win against [[Real Oviedo|Oviedo]] in the promotion play-off final, returning to the top flight after only a single season.<ref>{{cite news |date=23 June 2024 |title=Espanyol promoted to LaLiga after year away |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/40415431/espanyol-laliga-promotion-playoff-win |access-date=25 June 2024 |publisher=ESPN |archive-date=25 June 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240625044114/https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/40415431/espanyol-laliga-promotion-playoff-win |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |date=23 June 2024 |title=Espanyol promoted to La Liga with playoff win over Oviedo |url=https://www.thescore.com/esp_fed/news/2930578 |access-date=25 June 2024 |website=theScore}}</ref>

===Zamora Trophy===
The [[Ricardo Zamora Trophy|Zamora Trophy]] was awarded by newspaper ''[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]'' to the goalkeeper with the lowest goals-to-games ratio. A goalkeeper had to play at least 28 matches of 60 or more minutes to be eligible for the trophy.
